title: A scalable multiplexed Yeast-two Hybrid assay for protein-to-protein interaction screening
author: Chantal Nyirakanani
materials: Before starting the assay: Pour selective media plates (Corning 245mm Square BioAssay Dishes, cat. 431111) ~ one week before the assay to allow the plates to dry. If on the day of spotting the plates are still 'too wet' (if spots merge), dry the square plates in a cell culture hood. Preparation of SC-LW solid media (1L): Bacteriological Agar, Ultrapure Thermo Fisher Catalog #J10906.Q1 Uracil Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #U0750-500G L-Histidine Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #H8000 Ammonium Sulfate Fisher Scientific Catalog #A702-10 D-( )-Glucose Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #G8270-25KG Adenine hemisulfate salt Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A-3159 Yeast Nitrogen Base Without Amino Acids and Ammonium Sulfate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #Y1251-1KG Preparation ofSC-LWH+1mM3AT (1L): 3-Amino-1,2,4-triazole Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A8056-100G Day 1: Inoculation of transformed yeast cells Inoculate 5 µL of DBs 'glycerol stocks into 200 µL of SC-L medium, and 5 µL of AD glycerol stock into 200 µL of SC-W medium using a 96-well liquid handling robot or a multichannel pipette. If the alleles/WT pools are on the DB side (Y8930), inoculate an 'AD-null' strain (Y8800 with the empty pDEST-AD not containing an ORF) to help identify auto-activators. Note: depending on the assay version, the interactors, either in pDEST-AD or pDEST-DB, need to get cherry picked before the amY2H from the human ORFeome collection 9.1. At the same time, inoculate the 6 DB and AD controls in SC-L and SC-W, respectively (Dreze et al.). Incubate both cultures at 30 °C for 2 days. If your experiment involves many samples, a re-array step will be performed to organize the DB and AD clones, making the mating process easier. Day3: Step 2. Mating of Yeast Strains Combine equal volumes 5 µL of the DB and AD cultures into 180 µL of YPD to allow mating. Each mating is done in triplicates. All DB cultures should also be mated with the 'AD-null' yeast strain Perform the mating of control as well. Incubate the mixture overnight at 30 °C . Day 4: Step 3: Diploid yeast cell enrichment o Inoculate 180 µL of SC-LW medium with 10 µL of mated cultures. o Incubate the mixture overnight at 30 °C . Day 5: Step 4: Spotting on solid media o SC-LW: This is to select diploid yeast cells. o SC-LWH+1mM3AT: To screen for interaction o Incubate at 30 °C for 3 days. o On the 4th day, leave the plate at RT for overnight Day 6: Step 5: Take plate pictures, and Plate Scoring The steps are essentially the same as those used in pairwise Y2H. The key difference in the pooled Y2H approach is that multiple alleles are pooled and screened simultaneously against a single interaction partner, enabling high-throughput assessment of interaction effects. In addition, mating reactions are conducted in triplicate to enhance the robustness and reproducibility of interaction measurements. After step 5, continue to the following steps: Pick colonies from SC-LW and 3AT plates into 180 µL of corresponding liquid media SC-LW or SC-LWH 1Mm3AT. Make yeast lysate (see step 8). Keep one copy of glycerol stock as a backup in -80 oC . Perform PCR using barcoded primer sets. Pool PCR products and purify them Follow the sequencing company’s instructions for sample preparation. Seq Data Analysis. Indexed PCR for LW and 3AT plates PCR conditions: 98----2min 98------30 sec 57------10 sec 30 cycles 72---------ext time (30 sec/kb) 72-----------10min 12---------hold

Pre-chill the PCR plate and 50ml basin, turn on the 96-well heating block to 42 °C . For each LR reaction: Thaw 50 µL of competent cells On ice . MAX Efficiency™ DH5α Competent Cells Thermo Fisher Catalog #18258012 (or home-made DH5alpha competent cells Once competent cells are defrosted, transfer them into the cool basin and pipette 50 µL /well. Add 2.5 µL of the LR reaction and incubate 00:15:00 On ice . While the cells are incubating, add 500 µL per well of SOC media into a deep well plate. After incubation, heat-shock the cells at 42 °C 00:00:45 a and immediately chill On ice for 00:02:00 . Transfer all cells into a deep well containing 500 µL e SOC per well and incubate at 37 °C 850 rpm, °C, for 01:00:00 . Meanwhile, fill a new deep well plate with 1200 µL of LB-ampicillin. After incubation, transfer 250 µL of the recovery solution into the deep well plate containing 1200 µL LB-amp. In addition, we like to spot 5 µL of the recovery onto a 15cm LB-amp petri dish. This can help indicate the success of the LR reactions and transformation. Incubate the deep well at 37 °C 850 rpm, °C, overnight. The spotted 15Cm LB-amp petri dish are incubated at 37 °C overnight. Next day, make two copies of glycerol stocks (1:1 ratio of 40% glycerol and culture). Store your bacteria expression clones at -80°C. Spin the bacteria culture at 4000 rpm, °C, for 00:30:00 and perform 96-well DNA purification (following Qiagen protocol). Inoculate a single colony of desired haploid S. cerevisiae yeast strains to perform yeast transformations the next day: Y8800 (MATa) for allele/WT pools in pDEST-AD-prey plasmids, Y8930 (MATα) for alleles/WT in DB plasmid (plasmid details see table in step 5) --> pick one colony into ~ 50 mL YPD media and incubate at 30 °C 200 rpm, °C, overnight.

The next day, for each gene, a pool of 30 clones comprising 28 allele variants and a wild-type clone was created. To ensure adequate wild-type representation, twice the amount of the wild-type gene was added to the pool. An equal amount of each allele culture was combined to a final pool volume of 2 mL (in a deep well plate). S-Blocks (24), Deepwell, Deep well Qiagen Catalog #19585

For each replicate, we perform PCR with different forward and reverse barcoded primer sets (6 different sets in total). Therefore, each PCR plate contains amplicons with two unique barcodes and can now be pooled. For example, one 96-well plate of amY2H will become 6 plates (3 replicates, two media conditions). 3AT replicates will be pooled with LW replicates, then PCR purified (Qiagen PCR purification kit). After PCR purification, 1 μg of 3AT and 1 μg of LW samples are pooled and gel-purified (Qiagen gel purification kit). This step is crucial for removing unwanted by-products. The purified samples were sent to Plasmidsaurus for custom Nanopore sequencing.

Indexed PCR Phusion HF DNA Polymerase Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #F530L Gel of PCR products: 96-well Agarose gel following the manufacturers protocol E-Gel™ 96 Agarose Gels Life Technologies Catalog #G700801

PCR products Pooling and Purification Each well of each PCR plate contains amplicons with two unique barcodes and can be pooled into a single sample. The pooled products were purified by first using the Qiagen PCR purification kit, followed by gel purification (Qiagen gel purification kit). The purified samples were sent to Plasmidsaurus for custom Nanopore sequencing. steps.title: Inoculate entry clone cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate each entry clone (wild‑type and alleles) in 1 mL LB‑Spec medium (plasmid backbone pDONR‑223) and incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking at 850 rpm.

steps.title: Extract plasmid DNA from clones
steps.instruction: Spin the deep‑well plate at 4000 rpm (temperature not specified) for 30 min, then extract DNA using a 96‑well DNA extraction kit.

steps.title: Set up En Masse LR reactions
steps.instruction: Assemble En Masse Gateway LR reactions in a 96‑well PCR plate (full‑skirt, natural, 25/box, MedSupply Partners Catalog #15‑2844) using LR Clonase Mix II (Life Technologies Catalog #11791100) and the appropriate pDEST plasmid (assay versions 1, 2, 3 in two orientations). Incubate the reactions overnight at 25 °C.

steps.title: Yeast transformation and selection
steps.instruction: Transform haploid S. cerevisiae strains Y8800 (MATa) and Y8930 (MATα) with pDest‑AD‑prey (TRP1) and pDest‑DB‑bait (LEU2) vectors, select transformants, and generate glycerol stocks.

substeps.instruction: Harvest yeast culture at OD₆₀₀ 0.8–1.0 (mid‑log). If OD₆₀₀ is higher, dilute to OD₆₀₀ 0.33 with fresh YPD and grow at 30 °C for 3 h (≈ two doublings).
Pellet cells at 2000 rpm (temperature not specified) for 5 min and discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 10 mL sterile water, spin 2000 rpm for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Optional: wash a second time with 5 mL 0.1 M LiAc, spin 2000 rpm for 5 min, discard supernatant.

Resuspend pellet in yeast transformation (TRAFO) buffer prepared as follows (volumes for 1 reaction): 25 µL 60 % PEG 3350, 4.5 µL 1 M LiAc, 9.25 µL water, 6.25 µL 2 mg/mL ssDNA (total 45 µL). Scale proportionally for 50 or 100 reactions as needed.
Aliquot 45 µL TRAFO buffer into each well of a 96‑well round‑bottom Costar plate and add 5–7 µL of DNA from the LR reaction.
Seal plates and incubate at 42 °C for 1 h.
Spot 5–7 µL of each transformation onto selective agar: SC‑L for DB vector and SC‑W for AD vector. Incubate plates at 30 °C for 3 days.
After 3 days, pick colonies into liquid selective media (SC‑L for DB, SC‑W for AD) and incubate at 30 °C for 2 days.
Prepare two glycerol stocks per culture by mixing 1 part culture with 1 part 40 % glycerol (final 20 % glycerol). Store stocks at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare yeast lysates for QC
steps.instruction: Generate lysates from yeast expression pools for indexed PCR quality control.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.2 M dibasic sodium phosphate stock (Fisher Scientific #S369500): dissolve 53.65 g Na₂HPO₄·7H₂O in 1 L ddH₂O, adjust pH to 7.4.
Prepare 0.2 M monobasic sodium phosphate stock (Fisher Scientific #S373500): dissolve 27.6 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O in 1 L ddH₂O, adjust pH to 7.4.
Make 25 mL lysate buffer by mixing 20.25 mL 0.2 M Na₂HPO₄·7H₂O with 4.75 mL 0.2 M NaH₂PO₄·H₂O; adjust final pH to 7.5.
Add zymolase to the buffer (2 mg zymolase per 1 mL lysate buffer; Zymolase 20T, US Biological Catalog #Z1000).
Distribute 25 µL of the lysis buffer into each well of a 96‑well plate.
Add 6 µL saturated yeast suspension to each well.
Seal the plate with a heat sealer and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h (do not stack plates after sealing).
Heat‑shock the sealed plate at 60 °C for 5 min.
Add 80 µL sterile water to each well using an electronic Ovation multichannel pipette.
Store the plates at –20 °C and set up indexed PCR for quality control.
